turns.answer:
For keeping a Wi-Fi router and cable modem running during a power outage, you don't need a large power station. A small portable power station with 200–300Wh capacity is usually enough to keep your internet running for roughly 6–15 hours, depending on your equipment.

Most home internet setups consume:

Wi-Fi router: 8–15 watts

Cable modem: 5–12 watts

Combined: typically 15–25 watts

How long will a power station last?

Important: For seamless internet backup, choose a model with UPS functionality and test whether your modem and router stay connected during transfer. Also, a battery can keep your equipment powered, but your internet provider's network must remain operational during the outage.

One question: Do you want your Wi-Fi to stay running for 4 hours, 8 hours, 12 hours, or 24 hours during an outage? I can narrow this down to the smallest suitable model.
